strings: This ritualistic step marks the culmination of the shaman's ordeal at the Brazier of Everfount along the coast of Silverpine Forest. Having shattered the corrupt spirits threatening the spring with a burst of elemental radiance, the shaman stands before an apparition of pure water to receive its communion.

Upon reciting the final incantation at the Brazier of Everfount, an explosion of light scours the area of surrounding corruption. The hissed protests of tainted water drops evaporating over elemental flame fade, leaving the immediate shore silent as malevolent minor spirits disperse.

In the wake of the spirits' destruction, a Minor Manifestation of Water materializes beside the brazier. Grateful for the ritual intervention, the spirit recognizes the growing burden placed upon the Horde's shamans: though the local taint has ebbed, life in the decaying lands of Silverpine continues to wane, requiring vigilance to preserve.
What happens when the brazier ritual finishes?
Completing the incantation at the Brazier of Everfount releases an explosion of brilliant light. This destroys the surrounding corrupted spirits and purifies the immediate elemental flow.
Who is the Minor Manifestation of Water?
It is a minor elemental entity of pure water that manifests after the corrupted elementals near the Brazier of Everfount are destroyed.
water spirit silverpine | manifestation of water
What does the water spirit say about Silverpine?
The spirit expresses thanks to the shamans, noting that while this specific corruption has ebbed, life across the land continues to wane and requires constant stewardship to safeguard.
Where does this ritual take place?
The ritual takes place at the Brazier of Everfount, situated along the coastline of Silverpine Forest.
brazier location | call of water location
Why must shamans intervene in Silverpine?
As part of their elemental trials to earn the Water Totem, shamans must prove their commitment to balance by defending distant, embattled natural waters from blight and lingering corruption.
why shamans here | shaman duty silverpine
What comes next in the trials?
After conferring with the Minor Manifestation of Water, the shaman receives elemental remains or guidance to complete their journey and forge their Water Totem.
next step call of water | after water manifestation
brazier of everfount | call of water | elemental | minor manifestation of water | shaman trial | silverpine forest | water totem
This communion directly tests a shaman's resolve to heal suffering waters far beyond their native homes, earning communion with the spirit of water itself.
The Horde's spiritual leaders must cleanse corrupted waterways even within Forsaken-controlled territories like Silverpine to maintain elemental harmony.

Buzzbox 411 is an Alliance quest found along the windswept coastline of Darkshore. Operating through an eccentric mechanical relay network, the intoxicated gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle enlists travelers to gather coastal thresher eyes to bring his second research machine back online.

After assisting with the repairs of Buzzbox 827 further south, the voice of the gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle crackles over the mechanical transmitter once more. Stationed somewhere safely out of sight, Wizbang directs adventurers further north along Darkshore's mist-laden beach to locate another damaged terminal: Buzzbox 411. Between transmissions punctuated by hiccups and muttered praises of crawler wine, he reveals that local aquatic predators hold the components necessary to keep his coastal apparatus functional.

Restoring Buzzbox 411 requires diving into the chilly, turbulent waters off the coast of Auberdine. Darkshore threshers prowl the shallows, aggressive marine beasts whose ocular organs contain precisely the properties Wizbang claims are needed to recalibrate the device. Feeding the requested thresher eyes into the waiting hatch of the machine jolts the apparatus back into operation, rewarding the courier and opening the line for another increasingly slurred assignment.

Buzzbox 411 is a mechanical transmitter device situated north of Auberdine along the Darkshore shoreline. It serves as part of an experimental listening and research network maintained by the gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle.
buzzbox 411 | what is buzzbox 411 | buzzbox 411 purpose

Wizbang Cranktoggle is an eccentric gnome tinkerer who communicates remotely through the Buzzbox network. He spends his field research heavily enjoying crawler wine while relying on passing adventurers to do the hazardous fieldwork of collecting animal parts.
wizbang | who is wizbang | who made buzzbox
Why does a machine need Thresher Eyes?

Gnomish engineering frequently blends bizarre organic matter with mechanical components to perform unorthodox tasks. Whether Wizbang truly needs the eyes for optical sensors or is merely using them in biological research while drunk, he insists they are vital to repairing Buzzbox 411.
why thresher eyes | thresher eyes for machine | buzzbox eyes
Buzzbox 411 is planted right on the beach in Darkshore, located north of the night elf settlement of Auberdine.
where is buzzbox 411 | buzzbox 411 location | find buzzbox 411
Where do I find Darkshore Threshers?
Darkshore threshers swim in the coastal waters off Auberdine and along the nearby shores, easily found by swimming out past the surf line.
where are threshers | thresher eye source | thresher location
What happens after Buzzbox 411 is fixed?
Once Buzzbox 411 hums back to life, Wizbang Cranktoggle thanks you over the static, downs another drink, and immediately asks if you are willing to fix his next machine, Buzzbox 323.
next buzzbox | what comes after buzzbox 411 | buzzbox chain
auberdine | buzzbox 411 | crawler wine | darkshore | gnome | thresher eyes | tinkering | wizbang cranktoggle
Using organic thresher eyes to calibrate a mechanical transmitter demonstrates the eccentric, boundary-pushing methods favored by unconventional tinkerers.
Wizbang Cranktoggle represents the quintessential gnomish approach to fieldwork: bold innovation, peculiar component choices, and delegating the dangerous swimming to whoever is passing by.
Auberdine's sentinels keep a watchful eye on Darkshore's waters, though they typically leave peculiar gnomish contraptions on the shoreline to their own devices.

Buzzbox 323 is the third task in a field-research line along the coast of Darkshore, commissioned through a speaker device by the eccentric gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle. Players must gather Moonstalker fangs from local predators and deposit them into the humming contraption situated north of Auberdine.

After operating Buzzbox 411 further south, the voice of the gnomish inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle crackles to life over the speaker. Interspersed with the sounds of heavy drinking and slurred directions, Wizbang directs adventurers north toward Auberdine, pointing them to Buzzbox 323 near a road bridge. His research requires six Moonstalker Fangs, harvested from the fierce feline hunters roaming the shrouded forests of Darkshore.

Approaching Buzzbox 323 reveals a machine that chatters with static and faint muttering even before repairs begin. Once the requested fangs are placed inside its intake hopper, the machine violently rattles to life, noisily pulverizing the teeth to dust. Wizbang's boozy voice promptly resumes over the transceiver, celebrating the delivery before prodding the traveler toward the next machine in his scattered network.
Buzzbox 323 stands alongside the main road north of Auberdine, just near the bridge crossing the local river in Darkshore.
buzzbox 323 location | where is buzzbox 323 | find buzzbox 323
Who is speaking through the Buzzbox?
The voice belongs to Wizbang Cranktoggle, a gnome inventor stationed elsewhere in Darkshore who communicates through remote transmitters while heavily indulging in ale.
who talks in buzzbox | buzzbox gnome | wizbang cranktoggle
What does Buzzbox 323 do with the fangs?
Upon dropping the Moonstalker fangs inside, internal gears immediately grind them down into fine powder as part of Wizbang's automated biological sampling mechanism.
what happens to the fangs | why moonstalker fangs | buzzbox grinding
Where can I find Moonstalkers in Darkshore?
Moonstalkers and their runts prowl the shaded woodlands and hills bordering the road both north and south of Auberdine.
where are moonstalkers | moonstalker fang farm | moonstalker location
What quest comes before and after Buzzbox 323?
This assignment follows Buzzbox 411, which required thresher eyes, and directly precedes Buzzbox 525, which sends you to collect grizzled scalps from thistle bears far south along the road.
buzzbox quest chain | what follows buzzbox 323 | buzzbox order
Why does Wizbang sound so incoherent?
Wizbang is thoroughly intoxicated while giving instructions, pausing to search for his ale and taking loud gulps between sentences.
why is wizbang drunk | buzzbox voice slurring
auberdine | buzzbox | buzzbox 323 | cranktoggle | darkshore | fangs | moonstalker | wizbang
The Buzzbox series demonstrates automated material processing coupled with long-range voice relay, an impressive technical design despite its rough operation.
Wizbang's remote acoustic communication network showcases typical gnomish engineering flair—even if his personal discipline leaves much to be desired.
While native night elves treat the fierce Moonstalkers with reverent caution, gnomish science reduces their lethal fangs to pulverized machine fuel.

Buzzbox 525 is the final stage in a series of communicative machines scattered along the coast of Darkshore. Created by the eccentric gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle, the contraption demands animal remnants to function—while slowly unraveling the inventor's true, illicit ambitions.

After servicing Buzzbox 323, travelers receive garbled instructions broadcast straight through the machine's rattling speakers. Wizbang Cranktoggle's speech grows increasingly slurred, filled with drunken chuckles and rambling directions leading far south along the main road of Darkshore. He directs his helpers to hunt down the local grizzled thistle bears and deliver four of their thick scalps into the compartment of Buzzbox 525, concealed carefully behind a fence in the roadside brush.

Upon arriving at the hidden machine, the curious hum of machinery is drowned out by raucous singing echoing from within the iron plating. As the grizzly bear scalps are deposited into the receptacle, Wizbang finally comes clean about his network. The contraptions are far more than mere communications equipment: they double as automated micro-breweries and distilleries. Disdainful of the night elves' strict and abstemious customs in Auberdine, the gnome built his contraptions to distill forbidden woodland spirits—using animal harvest like bear scalps to brew potent batches of 'thistle bear beer.'
Buzzbox 525 sits far south down the main road from Auberdine. Wizbang tucked it away just off the path near a rustic fence line, partially concealed beneath bushes.
buzzbox 525 location | where is buzzbox 525 | buzzbox 525 find
Why does Wizbang want grizzled scalps?

Wizbang claims the scalps are needed to repair Buzzbox 525, just as the earlier machines needed crawler legs, thresher eyes and moonstalker fangs. The drunken song about thistle bear beer coming from the box hints at another purpose.
why grizzled scalps | buzzbox bear scalps | what are scalps for
Why does Wizbang hide the Buzzboxes out in the wilderness?
Wizbang placed the machines outside Auberdine and relies on travelers to reach them. The final Buzzbox reveals why he chose these secluded sites.
why are buzzboxes hidden | why hide buzzbox | wizbang secret
Who is speaking through the Buzzbox?
The voice belongs to Wizbang Cranktoggle, an enterprising gnome tinkerer who installed voice transmitters inside his Buzzboxes across Darkshore.
who talks in buzzbox | buzzbox voice | wizbang identity
Can Wizbang speak through the machine without the scalps?
Yes. Wizbang can speak through the machine before the scalps are added. His explanation for the requested materials comes when the task is complete.
is the buzzbox broken | did wizbang lie
What song does the Buzzbox sing?

Before you deposit the scalps, the speaker repeatedly chants a drunken limerick: 'Though crawler wine's sweet, and thresher ale fine, and moonstalker moonshine is grand. There's nothing so dear, as a thistle bear beer, and soon I shall have some on hand!'
buzzbox singing | thistle bear beer song
auberdine | buzzbox 525 | darkshore | grizzled scalp | thistle bear | thistle bear beer | wizbang cranktoggle
Wizbang's multi-purpose transceivers showcase typical gnomish ambition, blending complex engineering with questionable practical priorities.
The strict stewardship of Darkshore leaves little patience for reckless gnomish tinkering.

Talen, an elf camped near the dangerous Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale, seeks recovery of a lost relic. After being ambushed and run aground by vicious naga, he dropped his prized ancient statuette along the surf and needs an adventurer to retrieve it from the ruins.

The sunken ruins of Zoram along Ashenvale's northwestern shoreline have long attracted those curious about the ancient night elven past. Talen was navigating the shallows in a small vessel when hostile naga surfaced and tore into him with claw and trident. He managed to scramble ashore with bare provisions to make a hasty camp, but in his desperate sprint for survival, his most precious find was dropped into the sands.

The ancient statuette left half-buried on the beach is more than a simple souvenir. Talen considers it the entire justification for braving the monster-infested Zoram Strand. Upon its recovery, he reveals that the drowned city holds centuries of forgotten mysteries, and this delicate carving acts as a vital key to understanding what remains hidden beneath the tides.
Who is Talen and why is he alone on the Strand?

Talen is an elf explorer camping along the southern edge of the Zoram Strand. Driven by historical curiosity, he journeyed to explore the drowned ruins of Zoram, only to be cast ashore when vicious naga ambushed his craft.
who is talen | talen lore | talen ashenvale
Where did Talen lose the statuette?
Talen lost the carving near the shoreline north of his camp. It rests half-buried in the sand near an overturned boat and a fallen tree along the surf where his vessel was attacked.
where is ancient statuette | statuette location | find ancient statuette

It is an ancient night elven relic salvaged from the submerged ruins of Zoram. According to Talen, the carving holds historical and mystical significance, acting as a crucial key to unlocking the drowned city's lingering secrets.
what is the statuette | significance of statuette
Why are there naga at the Zoram Strand?

The coastline of Ashenvale contains ancient pre-Sundering elven ruins that sank into the sea ten thousand years ago. Naga have claimed the drowned structures of Zoram as their territory, aggressively patrolling the beaches against outsiders.
why naga here | zoram strand naga | naga in ashenvale
What happens after returning the statuette?

Recovering the statuette allows Talen to decipher more of the region's mysteries. However, dealing with the naga threat along the strand requires further action, directing you toward their leader, Ruuzel.
what next after statuette | quest follow up
The statuette lies along the water's edge in territory crawling with hostile naga warriors and shore-stalking beasts, making its retrieval perilous for lone wanderers.
is statuette guarded | enemies near statuette
ancient statuette | ashenvale | naga | ruins of zoram | ruuzel | talen | zoram strand
Alliance forces pushing through Ashenvale face threats not only from Horde outposts in the east, but from hostile naga staking claim over the western coastline.
The ruins of Zoram represent lost Kaldorei civilization from before the Great Sundering, making the preservation of artifacts like this statuette a matter of ancestral memory.

Shindrell Swiftfire of Astranaar charges Alliance champions with scouring the northwestern coast of Ashenvale, where an ancient ruined city lies. Naga have surfaced in force along the Zoram Strand, threatening to push inward from the sea. Halting their foothold protects the forest from a haunting echo of the night elves' distant past.

Northwest of Astranaar, where the dense canopy of Ashenvale meets the Veiled Sea, lies the windswept shore known as the Zoram Strand. Long quiet and littered with the bleached stones of a civilization torn apart ten millennia ago, the beach has suddenly teemed with serpentine horrors. The Wrathtail naga have slithered out from the dark tides, establishing a hostile beachhead right on the borders of night elven territory.

Beneath the pounding surf rests the doomed city of Zoram, shattered and submerged during the Great Sundering. For ages it remained an abandoned relic, nearly forgotten by the kaldorei. The sudden emergence of the naga among its ruins stirs bitter memories among the defenders in Astranaar. Sentinels like Shindrell Swiftfire recognize the serpentine invaders as twisted cousins borne of their own ancient catastrophe, and they refuse to allow the depths to claim the shore once more.

The Zoram Strand is the rugged northwestern shoreline of Ashenvale, facing the Veiled Sea. It marks the site of ancient Zoram, a kaldorei city swallowed by the ocean during the Sundering ten thousand years ago.
zoram strand | where is zoram strand | what is zoram
Why are the naga attacking Ashenvale's coast?

Their precise motives remain mysterious to the Sentinels in Astranaar. Whatever drew them up from the deeps, their military encampments and aggression make them an immediate threat to the forests, forcing the night elves to strike preemptively.
why are naga here | naga motive zoram | why wrathtails

Shindrell Swiftfire is a night elf sentinel stationed in the heart of Astranaar. She monitors regional threats to Ashenvale and organizes strikes against hostile incursions, including the naga upon the coast.
What history do the night elves share with the naga?

The naga were once Highborne night elves who served Queen Azshara. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Sundering, they were dragged into the abyssal depths and transformed into serpentine creatures, making every encounter deeply bitter for modern kaldorei.
naga elf connection | history with naga | shared history
What happens after clearing the Zoram Strand?

After thinning the naga along the strand, Shindrell Swiftfire redirects Alliance defenders to handle other emerging aerial threats along the border, sending scouts south toward Stonetalon to deal with vicious pridewings.
next quest | what after zoram strand | pridewings
Is the Horde also present at the Zoram Strand?

Yes. While Alliance champions hunt the shoreline's naga from Astranaar, the Horde maintains a fortified seaside outpost called Zoram'gar Outpost on the strand, contesting the region and battling both the naga and Alliance alike.
horde zoram strand | zoram'gar | is the horde there
ashenvale | astranaar | naga | shindrell | strand | sundering | swiftfire | wrathtail | zoram
The wind-battered coast and broken ruins provide prime vantage points for tracking the amphibious raiders as they emerge from the breakers.
Securing the western flank of Ashenvale prevents Astranaar from being caught between coastal invaders and encroaching Horde lumber operations.
Every naga slain on the strand is a grim reminder of Azshara's arrogance and the Sundering that broke the ancient world. Sentinels will never permit these twisted kin to regain ground in Kalimdor.

Ruuzel is an Alliance quest offered by Talen on the edges of the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale. After recovering an ancient Kaldorei statuette from the coast, adventurers are sent to wrest the Ring of Zoram from the naga leader Ruuzel to unlock its sealed secrets.

Before the Great Sundering tore Kalimdor apart and cast its grand coastal cities beneath the sea, the city of Zoram was governed by powerful night elven nobility. Chief among their regalia was the Ring of Zoram, a band enchanted to act as a master key capable of opening any lock within the city's bounds. Following the cataclysm, the ring was lost to the tides for millennia, preserving the secrets of sunken relics from curious eyes.

With the recent arrival of the naga on the Zoram Strand, the serpentine invaders began scouring the ruins of their former homeland. Ruuzel, the matriarch leading the local brood, successfully unearthed the Ring of Zoram and carried it off to her sanctuary on an island to the north. Seeking to unseal the statuette dragged from the shallows, the night elf Talen tasks Alliance travelers with hunting down Ruuzel and reclaiming the ancient heirloom.

Ruuzel is the leader of the naga occupying the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. She makes her lair on an offshore island to the north, guarding salvaged treasures of the sunken night elf civilization.
ruuzel lore | who is the naga leader | ruuzel boss
What is the Ring of Zoram?
The Ring of Zoram was an enchanted heirloom belonging to the ancient rulers of Zoram before the Sundering. It serves as a master key capable of opening any lock crafted within the city.
ring of zoram lore | what does the ring do | zoram key
Why does Talen need the ring?
Talen seeks to uncover the secrets inside an ancient Kaldorei statuette recently retrieved from the strand. The artifact is sealed with a lock that only the Ring of Zoram can turn.
why get ring of zoram | talen statuette lock
Where did the city of Zoram go?
Zoram was an ancient Kaldorei city destroyed during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Most of its grand stonework collapsed into the Veiled Sea, leaving only scattered coastal ruins.
what happened to zoram | zoram ruins
Ruuzel dwells on a large rocky island off the northern edge of the Zoram Strand, surrounded by her serpentine followers.
where is ruuzel | ruuzel island location
What happens after retrieving the ring?
Returning the ring to Talen completes his investigation on the strand. Grateful for your aid in unlocking the artifact's secrets, he rewards you and remembers your service.
what does talen do next | ruuzel follow up
ashenvale | naga | ring of zoram | ruuzel | sundering | talen | zoram strand
By slaying Ruuzel and aiding Talen, Alliance forces blunt the naga threat pushing ashore along northern Ashenvale.
Reclaiming the Ring of Zoram restores a piece of your ancestral heritage from the naga who desecrate the sunken ruins of your forebears.

Madame Eva of Darkshire offers to craft a protective ward known as the Totem of Infliction for travelers passing through the shadowed woods. By harvesting remains from the ghouls, skeletons, and venomous spiders haunting the region, she enchants a charm that retaliates against attackers. The task serves as both a grim test of survival and a superstitious safeguard against the pervasive darkness of Duskwood.

Within her candle-lit abode in Darkshire, Madame Eva peers past the veil into the fortunes of those who cross her threshold. Sensing impending danger and violence waiting patiently on the horizon, she offers more than mere divination: practical sorcery. By gathering ten ghoul fangs, ten skeleton fingers, and five vials of spider venom from the haunted thickets, an adventurer supplies the raw materials needed to construct a protective ward against Duskwood's ravenous predators.

Ghoul fangs steeped in necrotizing hunger, finger bones wrested from restless dead, and potent arachnid venom are woven together by Madame Eva's enchantments. When grasped in times of mortal peril, the totem radiates a magical aura designed to reflect cruelty, inflicting spiritual and physical harm upon anyone foolish enough to strike its bearer.

Madame Eva is a fortune teller and mystic dwelling in the embattled town of Darkshire. She interprets omens and brews protective wards for locals and passing adventurers attempting to survive the supernatural perils of Duskwood.
madame eva | who gives this quest | eva darkshire
What is the purpose of the Totem of Infliction?
The totem is an enchanted talisman meant to ward off assailants. Held when threatened, its magic retaliates against hostile foes who attempt violent acts against the bearer.
totem of infliction purpose | what does totem do | totem lore
Why does Madame Eva need ghoul fangs, skeleton fingers, and spider venom?

By utilizing the anatomical weapons and remains of the forest's most aggressive monsters—the bites of ghouls, the grasping claws of skeletons, and arachnid venom—Eva crafts a protective retaliatory enchantment.
why spider venom | ingredients for totem | why skeleton fingers
Where are the components for the totem found?

The components are harvested from the undead and beasts infesting Duskwood. Skeletons and ghouls haunt the cemeteries and haunted orchards across the zone, while large venomous spiders nest throughout the shadowed woods.
where find fangs | where to get materials | where are ghouls and spiders
What danger does Madame Eva foresee?
Eva warns that whispering winds speak of a looming threat waiting in the near future, specifically telling the adventurer that she foresees widespread bloodshed on their path ahead.
eva fortune | what danger coming | future bloodshed
Is crafting the totem considered dark magic?

While crafting items out of corpse parts and venom edges close to shadow craft, in the desperate environment of Duskwood, folk hedge-magic and protective charms are widely accepted methods of self-defense against the surrounding horrors.
is this necromancy | is eva evil | dark magic totem
darkshire | duskwood | ghoul fangs | madame eva | protective ward | skeleton fingers | spider venom | totem of infliction
Paladins may look askance at assembling wards from undead bones and spider venom, yet in the dire gloom of Duskwood, even holy warriors must sometimes reckon with pragmatic folk sorcery.
While Church of the Holy Light orthodoxy emphasizes faith and devotion, hedge-witches like Madame Eva channel spiritual will through tactile, grim talismans.
Warlocks will readily recognize the principles of retaliatory curses woven into Eva's protective charm.
In a borderland cut off from major military reinforcement, Alliance travelers frequently rely on the folk charms and wards of local mystics like Madame Eva to endure the forest's terrors.

Bathran's Hair is an Alliance quest offered by Orendil Broadleaf at Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale. Desperate to treat a mysteriously afflicted night elf child whose illness transcends the physical body, Orendil sends adventurers north to scour the ancient ruins of Bathran's Haunt for a restorative plant renowned for mending ailments of the spirit.

At Maestra's Post, just south of the Darkshore border, the night elf herbalist Orendil Broadleaf faces a troubling medical crisis. A young child in Astranaar has fallen grievously ill, exhibiting symptoms that resist ordinary physical remedies. Convinced that the sickness plagues the child's spirit rather than merely the flesh, Orendil seeks Bathran's Hair, an uncommon restorative herb historically gathered amidst the ancient elven ruins to the north.

The search leads adventurers to Bathran's Haunt, a ruined enclave tucked along the eastern side of the road leading into Darkshore. Gathering the bundled herbs proves hazardous, as Forsaken agents have infiltrated the ancient site. Returning the plants allows Orendil to brew a soothing draught, yet the discovery of undead interlopers operating openly in northern Ashenvale leaves the herbalist deeply unsettled.

Bathran's Hair is a rare medicinal plant native to the ruins of Bathran's Haunt in Ashenvale. Night elf herbalists value it for its potent restorative qualities, specifically its ability to soothe and heal ailments affecting the spirit rather than standard physical wounds.
bathrans hair plant | what is the hair | bathran herb
Who is sick at Maestra's Post?

No one at the post itself. The patient is Relara Whitemoon, a young night elf child in Astranaar and the daughter of Pelturas Whitemoon. The child's condition worsens by the hour, and ordinary remedies have failed because the sickness appears spiritual in nature, prompting Orendil Broadleaf to seek ancient botanical aids.
sick child maestra | who is orendil healing | who needs the cure
Bathran's Haunt lies in northwestern Ashenvale, north of Maestra's Post and just east of the main road heading toward the Darkshore border. The ruins are overrun with hostile Forsaken operatives.
bathrans haunt location | where to find bathrans hair | where is bathran
Why are there Forsaken at Bathran's Haunt?
No one knows what they are after. Orendil only learns of them when the herbs come back to him, and undead lurking so deep in night elf lands troubles him greatly.
undead at bathran | why forsaken in ashenvale | forsaken bathrans haunt
What happens after collecting the plant?
Once brought five bundles of the herb, Orendil prepares a medicinal concoction and asks you to rush it to the ailing child in Astranaar, beginning the follow-up quest 'Orendil's Cure'.
next quest after bathrans hair | what does orendil do with the hair | orendils cure chain
Can herbalists find the plant bundles easier?

Yes. The bundles holding the harvested plant lie scattered on the ground and can be difficult to spot with the naked eye, but adventurers trained in Herbalism can detect them using their herb tracking ability.
herbalism bathrans hair | tracking bathrans hair | plant bundle herb track
ashenvale | bathran's hair | bathran's haunt | darkshore | forsaken | maestra's post | orendil broadleaf | plant bundle
Securing medicine for the child in Astranaar reinforces the frontline settlements holding western Ashenvale against hostile Horde and Forsaken expansion.
The bundled plants scattered throughout Bathran's Haunt can be identified via herbalism tracking, making the search among the ruins far easier.
The encroaching presence of the Forsaken at Bathran's Haunt poses a grave threat to the sanctified borders of northern Ashenvale and the well-being of its children.

Deep in eastern Ashenvale, the night elf scout Kayneth Stillwind watches the encroaching Forsaken with growing alarm. Believing the undead are brewing blights to ravage sacred elven lands, he directs Alliance champions to raid an encampment near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den and secure a sample of their foul concoctions.

The night elves of Forest Song have long contended with satyrs, raging elementals, and orcish logging crews, but the arrival of the Forsaken marks a darker turn. Rather than merely felling timber, the undead arm of the Horde is establishing footholds near ancient ruins and sacred barrow dens. Their presence brings not only war, but the horrific specter of alchemical plague into pristine Kaldorei groves.

South of Forest Song, near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, Forsaken apothecaries and scouts have set up a fortified camp. There, amidst brewing caldrons and foul reagents, they bottle untested toxins. Kayneth Stillwind tasks scouts with infiltrating the camp to retrieve an intact Bottle of Disease so its volatile contents can be analyzed before the Forsaken can unleash it across the forest.

Kayneth Stillwind is an Alliance scout stationed at the outpost of Forest Song in eastern Ashenvale. He monitors hostile movements throughout the region, specifically tracking threats posed by the Forsaken and corrupting influences near the barrow dens.
kayneth stillwind | who gives forsaken diseases | forest song questgiver
Where is the Forsaken camp located?

The Forsaken encampment lies directly south of Forest Song, established in the vicinity of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den. The undead forces have gathered there around brewing tables and tents to concoct their biological mixtures.
where is the camp | where are the diseased bottles | dor'danil camp location
Why are the Forsaken in Ashenvale?

While the orcs primarily seek lumber and territory in Ashenvale, the Forsaken pursue sinister alchemical and biological goals. Operating near ancient Kaldorei barrows, they gather reagents and brew toxic compounds, raising elven fears that they intend to infect the land itself.
why forsaken in ashenvale | undead in ashenvale | forsaken motives
What happens after retrieving the bottle?

Kayneth Stillwind examines the captured bottle to identify its composition. His investigation immediately leads into discovering the plight of the sleeping druids inside the nearby Dor'Danil Barrow Den, prompting the follow-up quest Insane Druids.
what next | after forsaken diseases | quest follow up

Forest Song is an Alliance encampment and ruined night elf settlement in far eastern Ashenvale, situated near the border of Azshara. It serves as a vital staging post for night elf scouts watching the surrounding wilderness.
forest song outpost | what is forest song
What are the barrow dens in Ashenvale?

Barrow dens are sacred underground sanctuaries where night elf druids slumber in communion with the Emerald Dream. Dor'Danil Barrow Den is one such site, making the nearby presence of the Forsaken particularly alarming to the Kaldorei.

Long ago, during the reign of the Old Gods, primordial elementals blanketed the surface of the world, serving their dark masters. When those ancient entities were overthrown and sealed beneath the earth, the elemental spirits lost their tether to this realm, largely fading from physical existence unless bound and summoned by modern spellcraft.
